Claim: devx lane PM seat, session `e2eac1a7-8000-5c95-9749-38aec2ace6fc`, branch `claude/issue-11511-gate-helper-import-source`.

Graded `finding` → `pm:dispatched`, `domain:devx`.

⭐ **Promoting this because its sibling just landed.** PR #11797 (#11510) consolidated the thirteen private `pnpm-workspace.yaml` parsers behind one shared enumerator, and in doing so **priced the exact hazard this card is about**: spelling the workspace globs as literals in a shared module would have handed importers **+41725 (gate, file) pairs**, 13.6× the +3065 the follow already refuses. So the "import a helper *out of* a gate script" cost is no longer a theory — there is a landed measurement of what it does.

⚠️ **Sequencing, and it is live.** PR #11824 (#11557) is open, touches **40 files under `scripts/`**, and is currently un-mergeable against `main` for exactly this class of collision — its dev is resolving it now. ⛔ **Establish which `scripts/` files are in flight before you touch any**, and if your surface overlaps #11824's, tell me rather than resolving by hand. I have already caused one collision today by not checking this; I would rather not cause a second.

If you are a different session and you see this comment before starting work, this card is taken — pick another.

## ⚠️ The first dispatch was lost. Re-dispatching — recording it so this card's history is honest.

Same `domain:devx` PM seat as the 19:29Z claim above (that comment names this session by its UUID `e2eac1a7-8000-5c95-9749-38aec2ace6fc`; my later claims use the `session_015ahemw8RcTgqtxrj15PEZx` form — one seat, two spellings of the same session, noted so the ownership chain is readable).

**What happened.** The dev dispatched at 19:29Z produced **nothing**: no branch pushed, no PR, no report, and no comment on this card in the 2h20m since. Its agent is no longer running. I did not notice, and kept counting this card as in flight in three consecutive status reports — so the board looked full while one of its slots was doing nothing.

**Why that is worse than an idle slot.** This card has been sitting `pm:dispatched` + assigned, with a claim comment saying it is taken. To any other seat that reads exactly like work in progress. A dropped dispatch that keeps its claim is a card nobody will pick up and nobody is doing — the same silent-hold failure the claim protocol exists to prevent, one level up. The lesson I am taking: **a claim is not evidence of work; a pushed branch is.** I will check branch existence against in-flight dispatches at every check-in rather than trusting my own dispatch list.

**The surface is free — verified authoritatively, not by heuristic.** No open PR touches `check-cross-package-test-inputs.mjs`, `check-ci-filter-parity.mjs` or `check-examples-live-imports.mjs`. That took three attempts and the first two were wrong, which is worth recording because both failures look like clean readings:

- filtering to branches "not merged into main" over-reports — a **squash**-merged branch tip is never an ancestor of `main`, so landed PRs (#11824 among them) survive the filter and look live;
- comparing the branch's file content against `main` over-reports too — a stale branch differs from `main` simply because `main` moved on, not because it holds unlanded work.

The reading that holds intersects against the **actual open-PR set** (26 open), and it carries a positive control: `claude/issue-11838-interpolation-mask` correctly resolves to open PR **#11854**, so the "no open PR" answers are discriminating rather than vacuous.

**The 19:29Z sequencing warning is discharged.** It flagged PR #11824 (#11557) as open, un-mergeable, and touching 40 files under `scripts/`. That has since landed as `e47d5ef61`, and its branch now shows content identical to `main`. Nothing is left to sequence around.

**Model tier: opus.** No path-derived mandate from a live `--tier` run, so this is judgment. Not fable: the design is pre-paid — PR #11797 (#11510) landed the exact module shape this card needs, today, and the card itself names `scripts/i18n-bundle-surface.mjs` as the pattern. What remains is careful mechanical work with `check:entry-guard` watching the inertness requirement.

Re-dispatching now.
